## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `00a082a686ce195841e304eb9ee4fd4fbdc5c0c3`

Isolated, adversarial read of PR objectui#10828 for card objectui#10801. Inputs: the card and its three comments, the PR body, file list, diff and the head's check-runs (REST), the objectui#10533 precedent and the objectui#6140 / objectui#6153 rulings on GitHub, and the objectui tree at `refs/review/pr-10828` (fetched read-only) against `origin/main` `12809a595` (merge-base `95bad1236`; both files and `packages/types/src/select-option.ts` are byte-identical between the merge-base and current main, so the diff below is the whole change). The dev report on the card was treated as a set of claims to check, not as evidence.

Diff: 2 files, 35 insertions, 0 deletions, one commit. Each file gains exactly one appended paragraph.

### ① Derived judgments

**Installed spec, read from the head.** `packages/types/package.json` declares `"@objectstack/spec": "^17.4.0"`; `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves exactly one version, `17.4.0` (integrity `sha512-bOtSFih0…TmqoA==`). I installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0, 17.3.0 and 17.4.0 from the registry into a scratch directory; npm's 17.4.0 integrity is identical to the lockfile's, so the probes below ran on the bytes objectui installs. The registry's 17.x line is `17.0.0, 17.1.0, 17.2.0, 17.3.0, 17.4.0` with no 17.2.x patch, so "17.3.0 declared" is the exact boundary, not an approximation.

**Measured, one probe beside one control per key, on all three versions (`SelectOptionSchema`, `FieldSchema`, `ObjectSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, options with a two-character `value`):**

| Probe | 17.2.0 | 17.3.0 | 17.4.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SelectOptionSchema` shape keys | color, default, label, value, visibleWhen | + description (six) | + description (six); catchall `never` on all three |
| option `+description` | `unrecognized_keys[description]` | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED |
| select `FieldSchema`, option `+description` | `unrecognized_keys` at `options.0` | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED |
| `ObjectSchema`, select option `+description` | `unrecognized_keys` at `fields.status.options.0` | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED |
| option `+icon` (control) | `unrecognized_keys[icon]` | `unrecognized_keys[icon]` | `unrecognized_keys[icon]` |
| option `+disabled` | `unrecognized_keys[disabled]` | `unrecognized_keys[disabled]` | `unrecognized_keys[disabled]` |
| `rows: 4` over all 49 `FieldType` members | 49 refused by name `unrecognized_keys[rows]` | 4 accepted (textarea, markdown, html, richtext); 45 add exactly one issue, `custom` at `rows` | same 4 / 45 split |

The bare controls (option, select field, object, each field type without the key) parse on every version. Every spec claim in both notes and in the PR's measurement table matches this table. The PR's aside that a one-character option `value` fails `too_small` at `value` also reproduces on 17.4.0.

**6140 note, sentence by sentence.** "17.3.0 declared `rows` and option `description`" true. "this repository resolves 17.4.0" true. "17.2.0 refuses both by name, as above" true (rows by name on all 49 types, description by name). "From 17.3.0 `SelectOptionSchema` declares `description`, so an option carrying it is accepted and a select field or an object whose `options` carry it parses whole" true. "`icon` is still refused by name" true. "accepts `rows` on the four multiline editor types" true from 17.3.0. "on 17.4.0 every other field type refuses it by a cross-field refinement (issue code `custom` at `rows`), not by name" true (45 of 49, zero `unrecognized_keys`). "both may be authored there, `rows` on those four types only" true. "`select-option-spec-extension-7014.test.ts` in `@object-ui/types` re-derives both boundaries" true: the pin at `packages/types/src/__tests__/select-option-spec-extension-7014.test.ts` asserts the six-key set, `description` accepted on an option and through a select field, `icon` / `disabled` refused by name, `rows` accepted on the four types and refused with `custom` (not `unrecognized_keys`) on `text` / `select`, and the four inert editor keys still refused by name.

**7014-q1 note, sentence by sentence.** "17.3.0 declared it" true. "strict over six keys, `description` among them" true. "an option carrying it is accepted and a field whose `options` carry it parses whole" true. "`disabled` and `icon` are still refused by name" true. "'must never reach' now holds for `disabled` and `icon` only" true of the three keys that paragraph names. "the spec's new key reached both faces with no edit here" true by construction: `SelectOptionBase extends Omit` of the spec's `SelectOption` on `visibleWhen` (`select-option.ts:69`), the spec's `SelectOption` is `z.input` of `SelectOptionSchema`, whose 17.4.0 declaration carries `description: z.ZodOptional of z.ZodString` (absent at 17.2.0), and the form face `SelectOption extends Omit of SelectOptionBase on value` (`form.ts:412`). "the SDUI form face `SelectOption` gains an optional `description` too (nothing narrowed)" true and pinned: `select-option-tier1-convergence-7014.test.ts` records `PRE_CONVERGENCE_SelectOption` without `description` and asserts `assertionFormFaceKeptEveryMember`, `assertionFormFaceGainedOnlyDescription`, `assertionDescriptionIsOptional` and `assertionMetadataFaceGainedOnlyDefault`; `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*.test.ts` and is chained from the package `type-check` script, and Type Check is green on the head. So "exactly one key, on one face" and "`SelectOption` identically" do undercount, and the note is right to say so. The last sentence naming the two pins is true.

**Standing sentences.** Every sentence the addition makes obsolete is named by the note rather than left under the umbrella: 6140's "refuses `rows` BY NAME", "is strict over exactly {…} and refuses `description` BY NAME", "must never reach authored object metadata" and "never in an object document sent to the platform" (all named as "the sentences above that call these keys NOT a spec key and keep them out of an object document sent to the platform"); 7014-q1's whole EXTENSION paragraph for `description`, plus "exactly one key, on one face" and "`SelectOption` identically". Sentences left standing that remain true at head: 6140's "the four inert editor keys stay deliberately undeclared and are pinned so" (`field-types.ts:278-282`; pin lines 172-176), the 17.2.0 re-measurement paragraph (dated by version), "`RichTextField` and `TextAreaField` now read through the declared types" (only a comment mentions `as any` at head); 7014-q1's derivation and `value` widening paragraphs. Residual nit, not a defect: 6140's 17.2.0 paragraph still says the keys were aligned with "a `@objectstack/spec` schema member that does not exist" in the present tense; the new headline "the spec has since declared both keys" is the sentence that dates it.

**Still pending.** 42 tracked `CHANGELOG.md` files at head; 0 hits for "refuses `rows` BY NAME", "The convergence is an EXTENSION", "consumed-but-undeclared field-metadata keys", "Converge the two named select-option types" and "Dated note, 2026-09-27"; the lit control "Adopt `@objectstack/spec`" hits `packages/types/CHANGELOG.md` and others. Both files are still in `.changeset/` at head, beside the already-corrected sibling `7014-select-option-spec-claim-correction.md`.

**Frontmatter.** md5 of the frontmatter block, computed by me at merge-base, `origin/main` and head: 6140 `85cd680d4d100a0510146a1d8032b965` at all three; 7014-q1 `ecedb10c5189b2c8841ea736b67c3cc6` at all three. Diff hunks start at body lines 35 and 37; 0 deletions.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged. 6140 stays `'@object-ui/types': minor` and `'@object-ui/fields': patch`; 7014-q1 stays `'@object-ui/types': minor`. No `major` in either file, nor anywhere in the diff. Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Fixed Group Check and Changeset Overwrite Report are all success on the head. Nothing about what is released moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Form vs the objectui#10533 precedent.** `6235-mergedsort-wrap.md` on main: a bold "⚠️ Dated note, DATE — headline — objectui#NNNN." then what holds now, then "The rest of this entry is kept as the reading of this change". Both notes here copy that form exactly. Two stated departures: (a) position, appended at the file end rather than after the opening paragraph (in 6140 this reads as a chronological chain after the 17.2.0 correction; in 7014-q1 it follows the closing export sentence); (b) the precedent also re-tensed each falsified sentence ("At this change …"), which this PR does not do, so a top-down reader meets the present-tense refusals before the ⚠️ marker. Both are named in the PR body and the report, and (b) is offset by the note quoting the sentences it overrides instead of only the umbrella, which is the residual the objectui#10533 review itself recorded as non-blocking. Nit, not a defect.

**`Clause-②: no` is honest.** The diff is two Markdown bodies, 0 deletions, frontmatter byte-identical; no type, schema, export, runtime path or acceptance set moves. The prose is brought to the boundary the installed spec already draws.

**Dev's deviations.** (1) Widening the 7014-q1 note to "exactly one key, on one face" and "`SelectOption` identically": correct and necessary, since the form face gained `description` by the entry's own derivation and both sentences would otherwise publish false in the same entry the note sits in; same file, same paragraph, same cause. (2) "Four types, not two": the triage note named `textarea / markdown`; measured, `rows` is accepted on all four multiline editor types on 17.3.0 and 17.4.0, so four is the true reading and two would have shipped an undercount. (3) Placement at the file end: judged above.

**PR body.** Checked against the tree and the check-runs: the quoted sentences in the "What the note corrects" table are verbatim from the files; the frontmatter md5 prefixes match; "35 insertions, 0 deletions" true; the 17.2.0 / 17.3.0 / 17.4.0 table matches my measurements cell for cell; the `keyof SelectOption` eight-key claim follows from the sources and the pinned assertion; the 42-file pending check reproduces; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` does call a prose correction with identical declarations legitimate (its case 2), and `check-installed-spec-pin-claims.mjs` does exclude `.changeset/` (`:393`); the `SelectOptionBase` docblock does list only `label`, `value`, `color`, `default` as "from the spec" with `description` absent, and deliberately declines a longer enumeration. Nothing false found. One loose phrase: "`pnpm-lock.yaml` has exactly one entry, 17.4.0" (the lockfile carries a packages entry and a snapshots entry for the same 17.4.0; one version, which is the point). Local gate and test counts in the body are the implementer's words; CI is the evidence used here.

**Check-runs on the head (read after they settled, 2026-09-27 ~18:35Z).** 41 check-runs: 38 success, 3 skipped (`Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard …/4)`, `dependabot`), 0 failure. Successes include Build & E2E, Type Check, Lint, Test shards 1-8, Test (dist pins), Spec Main Shape Gate, Control Byte Scan, Line Citation Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard and the four changeset gates. The PR is still a draft.

**Measured vs reasoned.** Measured: every spec cell above (three registry installs, integrity-matched to the lockfile at 17.4.0), the lockfile and manifest versions, the frontmatter md5s at three refs, the diff stat, the CHANGELOG grep and its lit control, the 17.x version list, and the check-runs. Reasoned from source, not executed: the form-face `keyof SelectOption` claim (from `select-option.ts`, `form.ts`, the spec's `.d.mts` at 17.2.0 vs 17.4.0, and the convergence pin's type assertions that CI type-checks). Not re-run: any repo gate family.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-10801-changeset-boundary-correction`
Reviewed-by: `session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk`

**VERDICT: PASS**
